document.title: Self-hosted Sentry at enterprise scale
document.produced_by: Reference sample written in the Requirements Analyzer format (see ../README.md)

application.name: Sentry (self-hosted)
application.summary: Application monitoring: error tracking, tracing and performance, session replay, profiling, cron and uptime monitoring. The self-hosted package runs the full Sentry stack with Docker Compose and describes itself as 'packaged up for low-volume deployments and proofs-of-concept'.

components.name: Relay
components.role: Ingest edge: authenticates SDK traffic, applies quotas and rate limits, scrubs PII, writes to Kafka

components.name: Sentry
components.role: Web UI and API, ingest consumers, post-processing, alerting, task workers

components.name: Snuba
components.role: Query service and Kafka consumers in front of ClickHouse

components.name: Symbolicator
components.role: Native and JavaScript symbolication using uploaded debug files

components.name: Taskbroker
components.role: Kafka-backed task queue feeding task workers

detected_signals.signal: Kafka is the ingest buffer and event stream, with a 50 MB maximum message size
detected_signals.implies: Durable, replicated Kafka; broker limits must accept large messages
Analytical store sized for write-heavy, append-only ingest

detected_signals.signal: Raw event payloads (nodestore) on S3-compatible storage
detected_signals.implies: Amazon S3 with lifecycle expiry matching retention

detected_signals.signal: Files and profiles stored on a filesystem or S3
detected_signals.implies: Shared object storage instead of local disks so services can scale out

detected_signals.signal: Redis for cache, buffers, quotas, rate limits, TSDB and digests
detected_signals.evidence: sentry/sentry.conf.example.py: SENTRY_CACHE, SENTRY_BUFFER, SENTRY_QUOTAS, SENTRY_RATELIMITER, SENTRY_TSDB, SENTRY_DIGESTS

detected_signals.implies: Time-based expiry in ClickHouse and S3
Workers scaled on queue depth; no separate message broker needed
Dedicated compute and a shared cache for debug files
Metrics agent feeding the firm's monitoring
One organisation with teams and projects, managed through SSO
Internal use is permitted; offering a competing hosted service is not

scenario.summary: A large engineering organisation wants to run Sentry for 2,500 projects inside its own AWS accounts, because error and performance telemetry carries customer data and source context that may not leave the firm's environment.
assumptions: 5,000 events per second sustained and 25,000 per second during incident storms
About 2 TB per month of attachments, replays and profiles
Telemetry and backups stay in EU regions
out_of_scope: Sentry SaaS features that are not part of the self-hosted distribution

functional_requirements.statement: Ingest errors, transactions and spans, session replays, profiles, attachments, cron check-ins and uptime results from every supported SDK
Group issues, alert teams (email, Slack, PagerDuty) and create Jira tickets
CI pipelines upload releases, source maps and debug files for symbolication
Search issues and build dashboards across errors and performance data
Engineers sign in through the corporate IdP; teams map to IdP groups
Workloads in other AWS accounts send events without crossing the internet

non_functional_requirements.statement: Absorb incident storms without dropping accepted events
Ingest stays up through the loss of one availability zone

non_functional_requirements.target: Kafka replication factor 3 with min in-sync replicas 2; producer acks=all

non_functional_requirements.statement: New errors appear as issues quickly
non_functional_requirements.target: p95 under 60 seconds sustained, under 5 minutes during storms
Errors 90 days; spans, replays and profiles 30 days

non_functional_requirements.statement: Telemetry and backups stay in EU regions, encrypted with customer-managed keys
non_functional_requirements.target: 100% of stores use KMS customer-managed keys; 0 non-EU copies

non_functional_requirements.statement: PII is scrubbed before anything is stored
non_functional_requirements.target: Default and custom scrubbing rules enforced at Relay for 100% of projects

non_functional_requirements.statement: SSO with MFA for everyone; local accounts only for break-glass
Licence terms reviewed and the platform logged as an internal tool
non_functional_requirements.target: Legal approval of FSL-1.1 before go-live

non_functional_requirements.statement: Internal SDK traffic stays private; only browser and mobile telemetry uses a public endpoint
Kafka consumer lag drives alerting and autoscaling
non_functional_requirements.target: Alert when any consumer group lags more than 5 minutes

non_functional_requirements.statement: Storage cost is controlled with tiering and expiry
non_functional_requirements.target: ClickHouse data older than 7 days moves to S3; cost per million events reported monthly

non_functional_requirements.statement: Recover from regional loss using backups held in another EU region
non_functional_requirements.target: RPO 15 minutes for metadata, 24 hours for analytics; RTO 4 hours

between: org policy: prefer managed data services
policy_conflicts.summary: ClickHouse has no AWS-managed equivalent inside the firm's accounts, and the hosted ClickHouse service would move telemetry out of them.
policy_conflicts.proposed_resolution: Self-manage ClickHouse on EKS with the Altinity operator, S3 tiered storage and automated backups.

policy_conflicts.summary: Browser and mobile SDKs must reach an internet-facing endpoint, while firm policy discourages public data endpoints.
policy_conflicts.proposed_resolution: Internet-facing ingest only for Relay, behind AWS WAF with rate limits and per-project DSN keys; all internal traffic over PrivateLink.

policy_conflicts.summary: Sentry's producer allows 50 MB messages, which is above common broker defaults.
policy_conflicts.proposed_resolution: Raise message.max.bytes in the MSK configuration to match, and load-test the largest attachment and replay sizes before go-live.

open_questions.question: Which teams need session replay, and does replay content need extra masking beyond the SDK defaults?
Should client-side sample rates be enforced centrally through SDK configuration?

scoring.rubric: Mean of 12 parts: ten NFR categories (1 = numeric target, 0.5 = requirement without one, 0 = none), functional coverage, and conflict resolution; minus 0.05 per blocking open question. See ../README.md.
